stemMd: Twenty millilitres of 0.20 mol L⁻¹ HCl are mixed with 30 mL of 0.10 mol L⁻¹ NaOH. Assuming volumes add, what is the excess H⁺ concentration?
explanationMd: Acid supplies 0.020 × 0.20 = 0.004 mol H⁺. Base supplies 0.030 × 0.10 = 0.003 mol OH⁻, leaving 0.001 mol H⁺. Divide by the total 0.050 L to obtain 0.020 mol L⁻¹. Subtract amounts before calculating final concentration.

distractorRationale.e: This subtracts starting concentrations without accounting for different volumes.
distractorRationale.c: This confuses excess moles with molarity.
distractorRationale.a: This divides initial acid moles by total volume before subtracting neutralized acid.
distractorRationale.b: This is the base amount divided by total volume, not excess acid.
